summary: LLM token prices fell roughly 80% between 2025 and 2026, yet enterprise API bills continue to climb as usage explodes past $8.4 billion annually — the defining paradox of 2026 AI economics. Inference-time optimization routinely cuts total spend by 50-80% by combining prompt caching, semantic caching, model routing, prompt compression, and output control. No single lever is enough; the biggest wins come from stacking several, with prompt caching (up to 90% off repeated prefixes) and model routing (up to 16x cheaper per query) typically delivering the most impact for the least effort.

techniques.name: Prompt Caching (Provider-Native)
techniques.description: Stores the computed key-value tensors behind a repeated static prompt prefix (system prompts, RAG context, tool definitions) so the model doesn't reprocess them on every call. The saving is structural with no change to output quality — just order your prompt so the static part stays truly static at the front.
techniques.example: A RAG assistant passing the same 20,000-token knowledge base in every request moves that static block to the prompt prefix so subsequent calls bill cached tokens at ~10-25% of normal input cost.

techniques.name: Semantic Caching
techniques.description: Caches entire responses keyed by embedding similarity so that semantically equivalent queries return a stored answer instead of hitting the model. Complementary to prompt caching: prompt caching cheapens repeated tokens while semantic caching eliminates whole requests.
techniques.example: A support bot where 'How do I reset my password?' and 'password reset help' resolve to the same cached response, skipping the LLM call entirely for near-duplicate questions.

techniques.name: Model Routing (Frontier-to-Budget)
techniques.description: Classifies each query by complexity and routes simple requests to cheap budget-tier models while reserving flagship models for hard tasks. Budget models can cost 16x less for identical token counts.
techniques.example: Route 70% of traffic to GPT-4o-mini, 25% to a mid-tier model, and only 5% of genuinely complex queries to a frontier model, cutting a $3,250/month workload toward ~$195.

techniques.name: Prompt Compression
techniques.description: Shrinks the input by removing redundancy, trimming few-shot examples, summarizing history, and using compression models (e.g. LLMLingua) to drop low-information tokens while preserving meaning.
techniques.example: Run a 4,000-token conversation history through LLMLingua to compress it to ~2,500 tokens before sending, preserving answer quality while cutting input spend.

techniques.name: Output Length Control
techniques.description: Constrains generation with max_tokens limits, explicit 'be concise' instructions, and structured output schemas. Output tokens cost 4-5x more than input tokens, so trimming them has outsized cost impact.
techniques.example: Set max_tokens=150 and request JSON-only responses for a classification endpoint instead of letting the model emit verbose explanations.

techniques.name: Batch Processing
techniques.description: Submits non-urgent requests through provider batch APIs that process asynchronously within a time window (usually 24h) at roughly half the standard rate.
techniques.example: Send nightly document summarization jobs via OpenAI's Batch API to pay 50% less for work that doesn't need an immediate response.

techniques.name: KV Cache / Prefix Reuse (Self-Hosted)
techniques.description: At the inference-server level, managing the key-value cache lets multiple requests share computed prefixes in memory, boosting throughput and lowering per-token GPU cost for self-hosted deployments.
techniques.savings: 2-4x throughput improvement, lower effective cost per token
techniques.example: Run Llama or Qwen on vLLM with automatic prefix caching enabled so a shared system prompt is computed once and reused across concurrent sessions.

techniques.name: Code Mode for Agentic Workloads
techniques.description: Instead of passing verbose tool-call results back through the context on every step, agents generate and execute code that handles data locally, returning only compact results — dramatically shrinking input tokens in multi-step agent loops.
techniques.example: An agent querying a large dataset writes a Python snippet that filters locally and returns a 10-row summary, rather than injecting the full result table into context each turn.

tools.name: GPTCache
tools.description: Open-source semantic caching layer that stores LLM responses and serves cache hits based on embedding similarity, integrating with LangChain and major providers.
tools.pricing_paid: Free (open source; you pay for your own embedding/vector store infra)

tools.name: LiteLLM
tools.description: Unified proxy/SDK that routes across 100+ LLM providers with built-in caching, model routing, fallback, budget limits, and cost tracking through an OpenAI-compatible API.
tools.pricing_paid: Free OSS; Enterprise tier with SSO/support from ~$250+/month (custom)

tools.name: Helicone
tools.description: Observability and gateway platform providing request logging, cost monitoring, caching, and rate limiting via a one-line proxy integration.

tools.name: Redis / Redis Semantic Cache
tools.description: In-memory data store offering exact-match and vector-based semantic caching of LLM responses for low-latency, multi-tier cache strategies.
tools.pricing_paid: Free OSS; Redis Cloud from ~$5/month, Enterprise custom

tools.name: LangChain
tools.description: LLM application framework with built-in LLM caching (in-memory, Redis, SQLite, semantic), prompt management, and routing abstractions.

tools.name: Bifrost
tools.description: High-performance LLM gateway offering semantic caching paired with provider-native prompt caching, model routing, and Code Mode for agentic workloads.

tools.name: LLMLingua
tools.description: Microsoft prompt-compression toolkit that uses a small model to drop low-information tokens, compressing prompts up to 20x with minimal quality loss.

tools.name: vLLM
tools.description: Open-source high-throughput inference server with automatic prefix (KV) caching and PagedAttention for efficient self-hosted serving of open models.

tools.name: Portkey
tools.description: AI gateway with caching (simple and semantic), smart model routing, fallbacks, cost analytics, and guardrails across 250+ models.
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier; Pro from ~$49/month, Enterprise custom

quick_wins: Turn on provider-native prompt caching and move all static content (system prompt, tool definitions, RAG context) to the very front of the prompt so prefixes stay cacheable — up to 90% off repeated input tokens.
Add model routing: send the majority of simple queries to a budget-tier model (e.g. GPT-4o-mini) and reserve frontier models for genuinely hard tasks, cutting per-query cost 60-80%.
Set max_tokens limits and ask for concise/structured (JSON) output, since output tokens cost 4-5x more than input tokens.
Drop a semantic cache (GPTCache or Redis) in front of repetitive, high-volume endpoints to eliminate 30-45% of duplicate requests entirely.
Route all non-urgent, async jobs (summaries, classification, backfills) through provider Batch APIs for ~50% savings with no quality change.
